meta.title: Paint And SEEK! Maps

sources.label: Fans First Booyah - Paint and Seek tips for hiders and seekers

sourceNotes: Roster is exactly 4 maps (House, Grocery Store, Bank, Arcade), independently corroborated by four fan-wiki and creator-guide sources. No source mentions a fifth, seasonal, or unreleased map.

Single 'Maps' section by parent decision. With only 4 maps a Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced split would be lopsided and would assert a difficulty ranking that is not fully source-proven. Difficulty is kept as descriptive card prose instead.
No S/A/B/C tier or numeric tier is published. paint-and-seek.wiki references a 'map tier list' but the actual ranks were not exposed in fetchable text, so no tier is asserted.
Maps are in-round arenas, not separate Roblox places, so there is no placeId or API map metadata. Rows are editorial and source-backed from lighting/surface/strategy notes, not API-backed.
Per-map strategy is kept at the general source-backed level (lighting, surface, color match, outline control). No specific named hiding spots are invented beyond what sources describe.
Images are deferred to in-game capture and are NOT a data blocker. Every image field is null at this stage; the image gate will capture one screenshot per map and wire local paths.

items.name: House
items.cardSummary: A suburban home interior with tight rooms and patterned surfaces, the most forgiving starter map for learning how camouflage reads.
items.setting: Suburban home interior with furnished rooms, library props, and patterned walls
items.lighting: Warm and uneven, with softer pockets of light around furniture
items.bestHidingStrategy: Match the repeating room colors and break up your outline against furniture and wall patterns
items.difficulty: Beginner-friendly starter map; the busy surfaces and uneven light hide imperfect paint jobs more easily
items.seekerNote: Rooms read in a clear order, so sweep them one at a time instead of rushing
items.surfaceTexture: Furniture, library props, and patterned walls give plenty of texture to blend into
items.bestFor: Learning the basics of color matching and outline control
items.notes: Treated as the easiest of the four maps because its prop density and warm uneven lighting are forgiving to new hiders. Confirmed as one of the four launch maps across all sources.
items.verificationNote: Map name confirmed by four independent sources. Lighting/surface/strategy details summarized from Earnaldo and Fans First Booyah. Difficulty is descriptive, not a published tier.

items.name: Grocery Store
items.cardSummary: A retail supermarket of bright aisles and colorful shelf products, where the best hides borrow nearby product colors.
items.setting: Retail supermarket with stocked shelves, endcaps, and open aisles
items.lighting: Bright and flat across the aisles, with few shadowed pockets
items.bestHidingStrategy: Borrow the colors of nearby shelf products and endcaps so you read as part of the stock
items.difficulty: A clean, mid-range map; flat bright light is less forgiving than the House but the busy shelves still give cover
items.seekerNote: Sweep the aisles in order; the open layout rewards a steady, methodical search
items.surfaceTexture: Colorful shelf products and endcaps offer many color targets to match
items.bestFor: Practicing color matching against busy, varied backgrounds
items.notes: Bright flat lighting exposes mismatched paint more than the House, but the dense colorful shelving still supports good hides. Confirmed as one of the four launch maps.
items.verificationNote: Map name confirmed by four independent sources. Shelf-color and bright-aisle details summarized from Fans First Booyah and Earnaldo. Difficulty is descriptive, not a published tier.

items.name: Bank
items.cardSummary: A financial-institution interior of clean marble surfaces and long sightlines, the most punishing map for hiders.
items.setting: Financial institution interior with marble floors, clean walls, and open halls
items.lighting: Clean and cool, with even light that leaves few places to disappear
items.bestHidingStrategy: Control your outline and use side cover; smooth marble surfaces leave little texture to break up your shape
items.difficulty: The most punishing map for hiders; clean low-texture surfaces and long sightlines make a bad paint job easy to spot
items.seekerNote: Long sightlines reward seekers, so scan down the open halls before moving in
items.surfaceTexture: Marble floors and low-roughness surfaces give little visual noise to hide against
items.bestFor: Players who want the toughest hiding challenge and precise color work
items.notes: Described as the cleanest, least forgiving arena: long sightlines and smooth marble give hiders the fewest options. Confirmed as one of the four launch maps.
items.verificationNote: Map name confirmed by four independent sources. Marble/clean-surface and long-sightline details summarized from Fans First Booyah and Earnaldo. Difficulty is descriptive, not a published tier.

items.name: Arcade
items.cardSummary: A neon gaming hall of saturated colors and noisy visuals, the map with the highest skill ceiling for both sides.
items.setting: Neon gaming hall with arcade cabinets and saturated, busy decor
items.lighting: Bright and heavily saturated neon that shifts how every color reads
items.bestHidingStrategy: Manage both color and roughness against the neon so your paint matches the glow instead of standing out under it
items.difficulty: Highest skill ceiling; the saturated neon lighting can expose a bad paint job fast but rewards players who match it well
items.seekerNote: Bright saturated lighting can make a mismatched hider pop, so look for colors that fight the neon
items.surfaceTexture: Noisy neon surfaces and arcade cabinets create a busy, high-contrast backdrop
items.bestFor: Experienced players chasing the trickiest lighting on the roster
items.notes: Saturated neon makes color and roughness choices high-stakes: strong hides blend with the glow, weak ones stand out immediately. Confirmed as one of the four launch maps.
items.verificationNote: Map name confirmed by four independent sources. Neon/saturation details summarized from Fans First Booyah and Earnaldo. Difficulty is descriptive, not a published tier.
